extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, IP practitioners, and registered agents filing or prosecuting patent applications at ARIPO
extracted.subtask_description: Practical procedural and substantive requirements for filing, examination, grant, post-grant recordals and annuity/payment rules under the ARIPO (Harare Protocol) patent system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Member States and effect of designations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant designates the States in which it intends to seek protection; ARIPO receives, examines and grants the application unless one of the designated member states notifies ARIPO that a patent shall have no effect in that jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated States have six months from the communication on filing made by ARIPO to issue a written notification stating that a patent shall have no effect in that jurisdiction. Where a designated State objects, the applicant may attempt to overcome the objection (see Form 22A) or, if unsuccessful for that State, the patent may still be granted for the other designated States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusal by a designated State
rubrics_metrics.description: A designated State may refuse effect of the ARIPO patent in its territory on the grounds that (i) the invention is not patentable by the provisions of the Harare Protocol (i.e., patentability requirements), or (ii) because of the nature of the invention a patent cannot be registered or granted or has no effect under the national law of that State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a State raises such an objection, the applicant can file Form 22A [Notification or Request by Applicant to Designated State to Accept or Reconsider the Decision by Designated State that Patent or Utility Model shall have no Effect in its Territory] to try to overcome it; otherwise the patent may be refused only for that State.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT regional-phase entry time limit (ARIPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limit to enter the regional phase of the PCT in ARIPO is 31 months counted from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 31‑month deadline is longer than the majority of PCT contracting states (which commonly use 30 months) and must be observed for PCT applicants designating ARIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and document language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The office’s official language is English; the title, abstract, claims, description, and drawings of the invention must be in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No translations are required to be submitted in any of the designated States. A copy of the priority document must be provided with an English translation if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file via Form 3 and use a registered ARIPO agent
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent protection process in ARIPO is initiated by submitting Form 3 [Request for Grant of Patent]. The application is required to be submitted by a registered IP agent before ARIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 3 may be filed directly at ARIPO’s e‑filing platform, by e‑mail, in person, by registered mail or by courier. Note that a divisional application may only be filed with the ARIPO Office (not at a designated State).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents and evidence required on filing (accompanying Form 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing must be accompanied by: Form 4 [Appointment of Representative (Power of attorney)]; Form 13A [Request for Examination] (may be submitted with the application or requested within 3 years from the priority date); title, abstract, claims, description and drawings in English; a statement specifying the basis of the applicant's right to the patent (e.g., assignment); a copy of the priority document with English translation if necessary; and the receipt of payment of official fees (may be paid within 21 days from filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include required documents may result in non-compliance with formal requirements and issuance of a Form 15 refusal for formal non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of filing date (Form 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving the application, ARIPO issues Form 12 [Notification of Filing Date] informing the filing date and patent number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notification is sent to the applicant's representative and to the industrial property office of each designated State and triggers various timelines (e.g., designated States’ six‑month objection period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO conducts a formal examination to confirm compliance with prescribed formalities. If compliant ARIPO issues Form 13 [Compliance with Formal Examination]; if not, ARIPO notifies the applicant and Form 15 [Request to Reconsider Decision Refusing Application for Grant of Patent on Grounds of Non‑Compliance with Formal Requirements] must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 13 requests, pursuant to Instruction 41, that the applicant submit Form 13A [Request for Examination] if it has not yet been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting substantive examination and related deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination is requested using Form 13A together with lodging the search and examination fees; the request is deemed filed when fees and Form 13A are lodged. Where no request is made within the prescribed period, the application shall be deemed to have lapsed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to provisions, the applicant may request expedited or delayed examination by filing Form 48 [Request for expedited/delayed examination]. Applicants should ensure timely payment of search/exam fees to avoid lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination outcomes and applicant responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Following search and substantive examination ARIPO may issue: Form 18 [Notification of Non‑Compliance with Substantive Requirements and Invitation to Submit Observations and/or Amended Application] or Form 21 [Notification of Decision to Grant or Register].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Form 18 is issued the applicant is invited to file observations and, if applicable, an amended application together with Form 19 [Request to Reconsider Decision that Substantive Requirements have not been complied with] within 6 months. If refusal remains after reconsideration, the applicant may appeal to the Board of Appeal or request conversion into a national application under a designated State’s law via Form 23 [Request for Conversion of Application into National Application]. If Form 21 is issued the applicant must pay grant/registration and publication fees within 3 months to proceed to grant/publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated States' objection and challenge process
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated States may, within 6 months from notification of filing, raise objections stating a patent cannot be registered or has no effect under national law. The applicant can file Form 22A to ask the State to accept or reconsider its decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing Form 22A is the mechanism to attempt to overcome a designated State's objection; failure to overcome means the patent will not take effect in that State but may still be granted for other designated States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting, publication and issuance of certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon Form 21 [Notification of Decision to Grant or Register], the applicant must pay grant/registration and publication fees within 3 months. The patent application will then be published in the ARIPO Journal and a certificate of grant will be issued stating in which Member States the patent is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No special formalities are required at this stage apart from payment of official fees; timely payment is required to complete grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordals, corrections, transfers, and withdrawal/reduction of designated States
rubrics_metrics.description: Post‑grant or during prosecution the applicant may request: registration of licenses (Form 42); registration of assignment/transmission (Form 41); correction of clerical errors or alteration of name/address (Form 1); and withdrawal or reduction of designated States or of the patent application/patent (Form 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified forms for each type of recordal or correction to ensure ARIPO updates the register correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annuities (payment mechanism and calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annuities in ARIPO are paid directly to the regional organization rather than to each designated State. A late payment surcharge is applicable within 6 months. The 1st and 2nd annuities are paid upon filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PCT applications the annuity payment is calculated from the source PCT date (the year of the source PCT date is not included). For other patent applications the annuity payment is calculated from the date of filing in ARIPO (the year of filing is not included). Applicants must monitor annuity schedules centrally through ARIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official fees publication and currency
rubrics_metrics.description: Official fees related to ARIPO patent proceedings are revised annually by ARIPO and published on the Organization’s website; the applicable currency is USD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult ARIPO’s published patent fees (link provided in the article) for up‑to‑date fee amounts and payment instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application filing limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application may only be filed with the ARIPO Office and not in one of the designated States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants wishing to file a divisional must ensure it is submitted at ARIPO itself (and likely via a registered agent) rather than attempting to file divisional protection directly at an individual designated State's office.
